correctness.rationale: The three affine polynomials have degrees 15, 17 and 12 and their degree-17 homogenizations have no common zero: at A=0, G=-1, and at infinity the Y coordinate is nonzero. No constant linear relation is possible by the distinct affine degrees, so degree of map times degree of image is 17 with image degree bigger than one. The map is birational and gives the normalization. The fiber of [0:1:0] consists of the six simple zeros of A and infinity. In chart Y=1 the finite branches have ord(u,v)=(1,2), and the infinite branch has (2,5); normalizing the leading term of u makes the first odd Puiseux exponent 5, so the cusp has intrinsic delta 2. Independently expanding at a=A=0, let F=1+f a+g a²+O(a³), G=-1+B a²+O(a³). Reversion of u=Fa/G in v=a²/G gives v=-u²-2f u³+(-5f²+2g+B)u⁴+O(u⁵). Here f=0 or -2 by the sign of h³, f and g are fixed within a group, and B=1+ζ⁵ distinguishes the roots within that group. This proves exact contact 3 across groups and 4 inside either group. Substitution into the cusp uniformizer gives leading order 4 for each smooth–cusp contact. Thus delta is 2+6·4+9·3+6·4=77, multiplicity is 8, and the genus formula leaves 120-77=43 elsewhere. The line about distinct degrees refers to the dehomogenized polynomials, not their homogeneous representatives.
residual_risks: Only the singularity at P is resolved; 43 is a total, not a classification of the remaining singularities. The recorded symbolic checks are not a proof of contact orders on their own.
